extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, Medicare policy/finance staff, hospital reimbursement officers, and stakeholders preparing comments to CMS
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the proposed FY2027 Inpatient Prospective Payment System (IPPS) and LTCH PPS payment rules, including wage index transition policies, labor-related share proposals, and Medicare DSH/uncompensated care payment methodology. Intended to guide hospitals and stakeholders on eligibility, calculations, and operational estimates used in the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of wage index cap and associated budget neutrality (FY2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY 2027, we would apply the wage index cap and associated budget neutrality adjustment in accordance with the policies adopted in the FY 2023 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer readers to the Addendum of this proposed rule for further information regarding the budget neutrality calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional payment exception for discontinuation of low wage index hospital policy (FY2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to extend the transitional exception to the calculation of payments for FY 2027 for hospitals that benefited from the FY 2024 low wage index hospital policy and are significantly impacted by the discontinuation of that policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility and calculation specifics: the policy applies only to hospitals that benefited from the FY 2024 low wage index hospital policy. A hospital is 'significantly impacted' if its proposed FY 2027 wage index is decreasing by more than 14.2625 percent from its FY 2024 wage index. For such hospitals, the transitional payment exception for FY 2027 would equal the additional FY 2027 amount the hospital would be paid under IPPS if its FY 2027 wage index were equal to 85.7375 percent of its FY 2024 wage index. This transitional payment exception would be applied after the application of the 5-percent cap described at 42 CFR 412.64(h)(7). Example provided: comparison using numeric wage index values and the threshold (0.857375 × FY2024 wage index = threshold).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget neutrality for FY2027 transition policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to make the FY 2027 transitional payment exception budget neutral through an adjustment applied to the standardized amount for all hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: (1) the wage index cap policy would have mitigated decreases had effects been reflected solely in earlier years and (2) circumstances that led to declining to budget neutralize the interim FY2025 transition are not applicable to subsequent years. CMS proposes to use authority under section 1886(d)(5)(I)(i) of the Act to adopt the narrow transition and to do so in a budget neutral manner. CMS refers to past practice (e.g., FY2015 wage index transition budget neutrality) and states transition policies should not increase estimated aggregate Medicare payments beyond what would be paid without the transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital IPPS equivalent exception and GAF adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose a budget neutral equivalent exception under the capital IPPS because the capital IPPS adjustment for local cost variation (GAF) is based on the operating IPPS wage index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under capital IPPS CMS adjusts the capital standard Federal rate so the effects of annual changes in the GAF are budget neutral. Since FY2023 the GAFs reflect the wage index cap policy that limits any decrease in a hospital's wage index to 95 percent of its prior year value. CMS proposes for FY2027 to make a budget neutral equivalent exception under the capital IPPS similar to the operating IPPS transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed labor-related share for FY2027
rubrics_metrics.description: For FY2027, CMS is proposing to continue to use a labor-related share of 66.0 percent for discharges occurring on or after October 1, 2026, but to apply the wage index to a labor-related share of 62 percent for hospitals whose wage indexes are less than or equal to 1.0000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal baseline: Section 403 of Pub. L. 108-173 directs the Secretary to employ 62 percent as the labor-related share unless this would result in lower payments to a hospital than would otherwise be made. Implementation details: In the FY2026 final rule CMS rebased to a 2023-based market basket and finalized a 66.0 percent labor-related share for discharges on/after Oct 1, 2025; for FY2027 CMS proposes 66.0% generally but to apply 62% for hospitals with wage index ≤1.0000 and 66.0% for those with >1.0000. Cost categories included in the labor-related share are: Wages and Salaries; Employee Benefits; Professional Fees: Labor-Related; Administrative and Facilities Support Services; Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Services; and All Other: Labor-Related Services as measured in the 2023-based IPPS market basket. Puerto Rico: no Puerto Rico-specific labor-related share is proposed for FY2027; Puerto Rico hospitals are subject to national percentages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to qualify for Medicare DSH adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(d)(5)(F) of the Act specifies two methods by which a hospital may qualify for the Medicare disproportionate share hospital (DSH) adjustment: (1) 'Pickle method' (urban hospitals with 100+ beds can qualify if >30% of net inpatient care revenues are from State/local payments for low-income patients) and (2) the disproportionate patient percentage (DPP) method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DPP is the sum of two fractions: the Medicare fraction (inpatient days furnished to patients entitled to both Medicare Part A and SSI divided by total patient days for Medicare Part A beneficiaries) and the Medicaid fraction (inpatient days for patients eligible for Medicaid but not Medicare Part A divided by total inpatient days). Because DSH is part of IPPS, statutory references to 'days' are interpreted to apply only to hospital acute care inpatient days. Regulations at 42 CFR 412.106 govern DSH payment adjustment and counting rules; under §412.106(a)(1)(i) the number of beds is determined under IME rules at §412.105(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3133/1886(r) implementation: empirically justified DSH payment and uncompensated care payment structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning FY2014, hospitals eligible under section 1886(d)(5)(F) receive two separate payments: (1) an 'empirically justified Medicare DSH payment' equal to 25 percent of the amount that otherwise would have been paid under section 1886(d)(5)(F), and (2) an 'uncompensated care payment' equal to the product of three statutory factors described in section 1886(r)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS implemented the 25% payment operationally by adjusting interim claim payments to 25% of what would have been paid absent section 1886(r) and changing cost reports for settlement. Section 1886(r)(3) provides that there shall be no administrative or judicial review of any estimate of the Secretary for purposes of determining the factors or of any period selected by the Secretary for determining those factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1 (uncompensated care payment) — definition and CMS estimation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor 1 is the difference between the Secretary's estimates of: (1) the amount that would have been paid in Medicare DSH payments for the fiscal year in the absence of section 1886(r), and (2) the amount of empirically justified Medicare DSH payments that are made for the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS determines Factor 1 from the most recently available estimates calculated by CMS' Office of the Actuary (OACT). For the proposed rule CMS used OACT's projections based on the most recently filed Medicare hospital cost reports with Medicare DSH info, the most recent DPPs, and the IPPS Impact File, plus OACT's Part A benefits projection model (including projections of utilization and case-mix). Consistent with policy since the FY2014 final rule, these estimates will not be revised or updated after publication of the final projections in the FY2027 final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2 (uncompensated care payment) — uninsured rate adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor 2 is, for FY2018 and subsequent fiscal years, 1 minus the percent change in the percent of individuals who are uninsured, determined by comparing the percent uninsured in 2013 and the percent uninsured in the most recent period for which data are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS computes the second factor based on estimates of the total U.S. population, using census or other sources the Secretary determines appropriate, and certified by the Chief Actuary of CMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3 (uncompensated care payment) — hospital uncompensated care share
rubrics_metrics.description: Factor 3 is a percent for each hospital that represents the quotient of the amount of uncompensated care for the hospital (for a period selected by the Secretary) and the aggregate amount of uncompensated care for all subsection (d) hospitals that receive a payment under section 1886(r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS estimates uncompensated care using appropriate data, including alternative data where CMS determines alternatives provide a better proxy for costs of treating the uninsured (for example, Worksheet S-10 data). The third factor represents a hospital's uncompensated care amount relative to the uncompensated care amount for all hospitals receiving Medicare DSH payments, expressed as a percent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility rule: empirically justified DSH payment prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: Hospitals must receive empirically justified Medicare DSH payments in a fiscal year to receive a Medicare uncompensated care payment for that year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS makes determinations concerning eligibility for interim uncompensated care payments based on each hospital's estimated DSH status using the most recent available data; final determinations will be made at cost report settlement. For the proposed rule CMS estimated DSH status using the most recent SSI ratios and Provider Specific File available (FY2023 SSI ratios at time of development). If more recent data become available before final rule, CMS would use such data in the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classes of hospitals: eligibility and ineligibility for empirically justified DSH and uncompensated care payments
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS specifies certain classes of hospitals that are eligible and ineligible to receive empirically justified Medicare DSH payments and uncompensated care payments under section 1886(r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible examples: subsection (d) Puerto Rico hospitals; Sole community hospitals (SCHs) paid under the IPPS Federal rate (receive interim payments based on estimates subject to settlement); Medicare-dependent, small rural hospitals (MDHs) paid based on IPPS Federal rate are eligible if their DPP≥15%; TEAM model participants and CJR-X model participants (paid under IPPS) are eligible. Ineligible examples: Maryland hospitals (not paid under IPPS due to AHEAD model), SCHs paid under hospital-specific rates, hospitals participating in the Rural Community Hospital Demonstration Program (not paid under IPPS) — these are excluded from empirically justified DSH and uncompensated care payments. CMS describes operational details for SCHs, MDHs, and demonstration program participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental payment for IHS/Tribal and Puerto Rico hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS established a supplemental payment for IHS/Tribal hospitals and hospitals located in Puerto Rico to mitigate the impact of discontinuing low-income insured days as a proxy for uncompensated care costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology: the supplemental payment for a fiscal year is the difference between the hospital's base year amount and its uncompensated care payment as determined under §412.106(g)(1). Base year amount = hospital's FY2022 uncompensated care payment adjusted by one plus the percent change in the total uncompensated care amount between the applicable fiscal year and FY2022, where total uncompensated care amount for a fiscal year is determined as the product of Factor 1 and Factor 2. If base year amount ≤ current uncompensated care payment, no supplemental payment is made. Eligibility and payment processes align with interim and final uncompensated care payment determination; MAC will make final eligibility determinations in conjunction with final DSH/uncompensated care determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational projection practices and data sources for DSH/Factor1 calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: For projection of Medicare DSH payments and related estimates used in Factor 1, CMS uses the most recently available projections calculated by OACT that rely on most recently filed hospital cost reports with DSH information, most recent DPPs, the IPPS Impact File, and OACT's Part A benefits projection model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projections additionally require projections of expected increases in utilization and case-mix. CMS states these estimates will not be revised after publication of final projections in the FY2027 final rule.
